problem: VLN-CE agents assume correct instructions, while users often make mistakes (wrong direction, room, object). The prior IEDL detector/localizer works only offline after the episode ends, so agent and user cannot recover errors during navigation.
motivation: Human spatial cognition is imperfect, so real instructions contain errors that derail navigation. An agent that detects and localizes errors online can ask a focused question at the right time, improving success without overloading the user with queries.
key_idea: Run the pre-trained IEDL detection and localization heads online on partial observations during VLN-CE navigation, and ask the user to verify only the localized suspicious word, then re-encode the corrected instruction.
insight: Always Ask gets the highest SR but the worst interaction load (MIN 3.70), while I2EDL reaches similar SIN with far fewer interactions (MIN 0.90 vs 3.70), so gains come from asking selectively. The SR upper bound (60.1 avg vs 55.4 without interaction) and the delayed-correction experiment show that early detection matters, especially for Direction and All errors. The gain in SR from interaction is small (about +0.7 avg), so the detector's accuracy is the bottleneck.
method: Task IVLN-CE: the agent may query the user at any step about a token (with context window ς_l); the user returns the correct token if a real error lies within ±τ_l tokens of the predicted location.
Policy: a frozen BEVBert (SOTA VLN-CE) with topological and metric maps; not retrained, and the approach is model-agnostic.
Detection: from step p=4 onward, the IEDL detection head f_d outputs an alignment score, and a detection is triggered when a ≥ τ_d=0.6.

Localization: upon detection, softmax over the IEDL localization head f_l gives the most likely erroneous token; the agent asks 'I think there is an error in this part: <part>, specifically <token>. Is this the case?'.
Correction: if the error is within tolerance, the correct token replaces the wrong one and the instruction embedding is recomputed; otherwise nothing changes and navigation resumes.
SIN metric: SIN = mean of S_i / (1 + λ·N_int/max(1,N_err)) with λ=0.01, which equals SR when there are no interactions and penalizes false positives and repeated queries.
Baselines: Random Interaction (random detection and token each step) and Always Ask (asks every step from p=4 with a random token).

setting.backbone: BEVBert (frozen policy) + pre-trained IEDL cross-modal transformer with detection and localization heads
setting.training_data: No new training; uses the pre-trained BEVBert policy and IEDL trained on R2RIE-CE
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D images (panoramic via BEVBert) plus the text instruction
setting.action_space: low-level Forward 0.25m, Turn Left 15°, Turn Right 15°, Stop (BEVBert selects topological nodes, executed as low-level actions)
setting.privileged: Simulated oracle user who returns the correct token if the error lies within ±τ_l tokens of the prediction

numbers.extra: τ_d=0.6, τ_l=1, λ=0.01, p=4; simulated oracle user; 50% correct / 50% perturbed episodes

numbers_note: Table only reports R2RIE-CE Val Unseen; per-error-type rows for Room, Object and Room&Object exist but only Direction and All are listed here. Step-wise curves are only in figures.
results: I2EDL reaches avg SIN 55.9 with MIN 0.90, versus Random Interaction (SIN 55.2, MIN 1.84) and Always Ask (SIN 55.0, MIN 3.70). SR improves from 55.4 (no interaction) to 56.1, below the SR upper bound of 60.1 with correct instructions.
limitations: Gains in SR are small (+0.7 avg) and Direction errors remain hard, with no SR gain there.
The user is simulated by an oracle and only word-level replacement is handled; no real human study or cognitive load measurement.
The baselines are weak (random), and there is no comparison with other interactive VLN methods.
